related_questions.question: What is moyamoya disease of the brain?

text_blocks.snippet: Moyamoya disease is a rare, progressive cerebrovascular disorder where the main arteries supplying blood to the brain narrow and become blocked, leading to reduced blood flow. This forces the brain to create a network of small, fragile blood vessels to compensate, which appear like a "puff of smoke" on angiograms, hence the name "moyamoya".
snippet_highlighted_words: a rare, progressive cerebrovascular disorder where the main arteries supplying blood to the brain narrow and become blocked, leading to reduced blood flow

list.title: Progressive narrowing:
list.snippet: The carotid arteries, which bring oxygenated blood to the brain, gradually narrow, causing a decrease in blood flow.

list.title: Compensation network:
list.snippet: The brain forms a network of tiny, abnormal blood vessels (moyamoya vessels) in an attempt to compensate for the reduced blood flow.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Moyamoya disease can lead to transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), strokes, seizures, headaches, and cognitive decline.

list.title: Age of onset:
list.snippet: It often occurs in childhood (around age 5) or in adulthood (30s and 40s).

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: While there's no cure, treatment focuses on preventing strokes and brain damage, often through surgical revascularization to improve blood flow.

list.title: Surgical intervention:
list.snippet: Revascularization surgery bypasses blocked arteries, improving blood flow.

list.title: Associated conditions:
list.snippet: Moyamoya can also be associated with other conditions like neurofibromatosis type 1, sickle cell disease, and Graves' disease, in which case it's referred to as moyamoya syndrome.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Diagnosis typically involves cerebral angiography to visualize the blood vessels in the brain.
